text:
San Jose arrives in Los Angeles having lost four of its last five, outscored 17-9 in that stretch, and playing without Igor Chernyshov and Alexander Wennberg. The Sharks fell 2-1 to Calgary on Monday despite taking 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and William Stromgren scored his first NHL goal. The Kings, on three days' rest, are 2-3-0 in their last five and without Mats Zuccarello. With him out, Artemi Panarin has moved beside Haula and Laferriere and Martin Chromiak is on the first power-play unit. The teams went to overtime on Oct 3, a game San Jose won 5-4.

Neither side has controlled chances at five on five (SJS 44% of expected goals, LAK 49%). The matchup to watch is Los Angeles's power play, which creates 0.79 expected goals a game, against a San Jose penalty kill allowing 0.88. In net, projected starter Yaroslav Askarov is +7.7 goals saved above expected this season (saves beyond what the shots should have produced) after a -19.4 last year. Projected Kings starter Darcy Kuemper is -3.7, and -6.8 a year ago.

Panarin is 41% to score and 79% for a point. Macklin Celebrini, the No. 1 pick in 2024, is 40% to score and 79% for a point. Mason Marchment is one goal from 100 in the NHL. Adrian Kempe is day-to-day but could return. Our under-the-radar pick is Alex Laferriere, 60% for a point on more ice time (21:04 projected) against a Sharks team that gives up the most expected goals per 60.
